prompt:
report.py in the workspace is a rough first draft of our sales report tool. It reads a CSV of sales rows and prints revenue per category, but it breaks on real exports. Rewrite or fix it so it meets every requirement below. It runs as `python report.py INPUT.csv [--out FILE] [--delimiter CHAR] [--sort MODE] [--top N] [--bad-rows FILE]` (the options may come before or after INPUT.csv, in any order), uses only the Python standard library, and sample.csv shows the basic input.

Input: a header row, then one record per sale. The columns category, quantity and price must be in the header, matched case insensitively after trimming spaces, in any order. Other columns are ignored.

Requirements:
1. The input is RFC 4180 CSV. Quoted fields may contain commas, doubled quotes ("") and line breaks. Lines may end in LF or CRLF.
2. The file is UTF-8, and it may start with a byte order mark. If a required column is missing, write one line `error: missing column: <name>` to stderr for each missing column (order: category, quantity, price), write nothing to stdout, and exit with code 2.
3. A record is bad and is skipped when, checked in this order: it does not have the same number of fields as the header (`wrong number of fields`); its category is empty after trimming (`empty category`); its quantity after trimming is not a whole number of digits only, zero allowed (`invalid quantity`); its price after trimming is not digits with an optional decimal point followed by more digits, so no sign, no thousands separators, no exponent and no leading bare point (`invalid price`). For each bad record write `row <N>: <reason>` to stderr, where N is the 1 based number of the record among the data records. Completely blank lines are ignored and do not count as records, and a quoted field that spans several lines is one record. The other records are still reported.
4. Revenue is quantity times price per record. Use exact decimal arithmetic, not floats. Category names are trimmed of surrounding spaces and then grouped case sensitively. A category's revenue is rounded to 2 decimals only when it is printed, rounding halves up (0.125 prints as 0.13, 1.005 as 1.01, 2.505 as 2.51).
5. The output is CSV with the header `category,items,quantity,revenue`, then one row per category, then a final row `TOTAL,<items>,<quantity>,<revenue>`. items is the number of good records in the category and quantity is the sum of quantities. revenue always has exactly 2 decimals and no thousands separators. The TOTAL revenue is the exact sum of all revenue rounded once at the end with the same half up rule. It is not the sum of the rounded category values (three categories of 0.005 print 0.01 each and the total prints 0.02).
6. Category rows are sorted by exact revenue, largest first. Ties are broken by category name ascending ignoring case (compare the casefolded names), and if those are equal too, by the name as written in ordinal order (so "Alpha" comes before "alpha"). Revenue is compared as a number, not as text.
7. Output fields are quoted the way a CSV writer does it (quoted only when they contain a comma, a double quote or a line break, with quotes doubled). Every line ends in LF, including the last one.
8. Output is written as UTF-8 with no byte order mark, to stdout or to the --out file, whatever the console code page is, and category names with non ASCII characters must come out unchanged. With --out, nothing is written to stdout, and the file holds exactly what stdout would have held. Messages for bad rows still go to stderr.
9. Exit codes: 0 when every record was good, 1 when at least one record was skipped (the report is still written), 2 for any problem that stops the report: no arguments, an input file that cannot be read or is not valid UTF-8 (`error: cannot read <path>` on stderr), an input with no header row at all (`error: input has no header row`), a missing column, or an invalid value for --delimiter, --sort or --top (see requirements 11, 14 and 15). On exit code 2 nothing is written to stdout and no output file is created (this includes the --out file and the --bad-rows file).
10. A file with only a header row, or with a header and blank lines, gives the header line and `TOTAL,0,0,0.00` and exit code 0.
11. `--delimiter CHAR` sets the delimiter of the input. CHAR is a single character, or the word `tab` for a tab character. The default is a comma. A CHAR that is anything else, or is a double quote, a carriage return or a line feed, gives `error: invalid --delimiter` on stderr and exit code 2. Quoting rules from requirement 1 still apply with the chosen delimiter. The output always uses commas.
12. The input may have an optional `discount` column, found the same way as the required columns (it is not an error when it is absent). It is a percentage. When its value after trimming is empty it counts as 0. Otherwise it must be digits with an optional decimal point followed by more digits and must not be greater than 100, or the record is bad with the reason `invalid discount`, checked after the price. A record's revenue is then quantity times price times (100 minus discount) divided by 100, still in exact decimal arithmetic (quantity 3, price 10.00, discount 12.5 is 26.25).
13. If a required or optional column name appears more than once in the header (after trimming and ignoring case), the first occurrence is the one used.
14. `--sort MODE` chooses the order of the category rows. MODE is `revenue` (the default, requirement 6), `name` (category name ascending, ignoring case by casefolding, then in ordinal order), or `items` (items descending, then exact revenue descending, then name as in `name`). Any other MODE is a usage error and exits with code 2.
15. `--top N` keeps only the first N category rows in the chosen order. N is a whole number of at least 1, anything else gives `error: invalid --top` on stderr and exit code 2. When there are more than N categories, one extra row follows them with the name `Other`, its items and quantity the sums for all the categories left out, and its revenue the exact sum for those categories rounded once with the half up rule. The TOTAL row still covers every category. When there are N categories or fewer there is no Other row.
16. `--bad-rows FILE` writes a CSV file, UTF-8 with LF line ends and no byte order mark, with the header `row,reason` and one line per skipped record in the same order and with the same N and reason as the stderr messages. When no record was skipped the file holds only the header line. The file is written whenever the report is written, whether the exit code is 0 or 1.
17. The input path `-` means the input is read from standard input, with the same rules as a file (an input that is not valid UTF-8 gives `error: cannot read -`).

Check your work on inputs you write yourself, including ones with non ASCII names and with --out, because the tool will be run with a pipe for stdout.
